chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in

A man who performed *zihar* with his wife four times in one session, he said: 'Upon him is one expiation.' The meaning in this report is that we interpret it as meaning he bears one expiation in kind, which does not differ, just as the expiations differ in matters other than *zihar*; and the intended meaning is not that he bears one expiation for the many times.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on expiation for multiple zihar instances in one session?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies the juristic nuance of performing *zihar* multiple times in one session, ruling that the 'one expiation' mentioned refers to a single type of expiation (kaffarat al-jins) rather than a single act covering all instances. This distinction highlights the cumulative nature of the obligation in Shia fiqh, differentiating it from other expiations where multiple acts might be covered by one. The ruling underscores the importance of precise legal interpretation in resolving apparent contradictions in hadith reports.
